# The Stars That Burst in Praise

## Scripture
*"Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you shining stars. Praise him, you highest heavens and you waters above the skies. Let them praise the name of the Lord, for at his command they were created."* — Psalm 148:3–5

## Reflection

November's longer nights bring the Leonid meteor shower—fleeting streaks of light that flash across the darkness and vanish. These meteors are tiny debris from comet Tempel-Tuttle, burning up in Earth's atmosphere. They appear random, unpredicted, almost like the sky itself is breaking into sudden bursts of joy.

Psalm 148 calls all creation to praise—not just the steady stars that keep their places, but everything that shines. The psalmist doesn't limit praise to the predictable. He summons "all you shining stars" to join the chorus. If a meteor's brief flash can glorify God, how much more can our fleeting moments of faithfulness?

We often measure our lives by duration—how long we serve, how consistently we show up. But the meteor reminds us that praise can be momentary and still matter. A single act of kindness, a word spoken in season, a moment of worship in the midst of ordinary days—these flashes matter. They are not wasted.

God created even the smallest particles to burn bright. When you see a meteor streak across the November sky, let it remind you: your brief moments of praise are part of a chorus larger than you can imagine, joining sun, moon, and every shining star.

## Prayer

Lord of the heavens, thank You for the reminder that even fleeting moments of praise reflect Your glory. Help us not to despise small acts of faithfulness or brief moments of worship. May our lives—however brief or quiet—join the cosmic chorus that declares Your worth. In Jesus' name, amen.
